**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
 LeaseLocks are not being released properly due to incorrect construction of LeaderElectionRecords.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/issues/762
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/88194

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
Previous MR/Discussions:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88925
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88192

Both waiting for tests for several months.

One of the issues with writing a test for it was that fake client doesn't execute following validation (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4cc44fbef626e87e59f7e9e7bd0bf9ec447a3c39/pkg/apis/coordination/validation/validation.go#L43)
so I had to fake it in reactor. Not ideal but I have no idea how to improve it. 

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
No


review_comments: add test cases for the other scenarios please (thank you for adding a test)

sorry, which other scenarios? the test included is triggered in case of the original issue (LeaseDurationSeconds not being set) which in real life situation is triggered by the server validation. I can add other types of locking mechanism, but since we are faking validation through reactors it wont have a lot of value imho.

`acquire and lease from object without defaults set`, `acquire and lease from object with defaults set`, `acquire and lease from object with non-default values set` are all scenarios i'd expect to see

Generally rather than creating reactors like this we'd have a function that initialized the client, i.e. `newClient: func() *fake.ClientSet { ... create client and setup arbitrary reactors }` which enables you to build more complex setup.

Ideally it seems like we should use something like Server Side Apply to only change the LeaderTransitions fields. 

I may be missing something, but the use case for this code seems to be we have lost the lease. We (eg. identity baz) were the leader but lost the lease (we no longer hold the lock) and are trying to record a bump in the number of transitions. Recoding the bump in transitions is failing because we don't allow a lease to have a duration of 0 and we are setting it to zero because that is the default value for that field. Your fixing that by using the duration set by the current owner (not us, example holder identity zat) to the new record we are writing. It seems like since we didn't explicitly set the holder identity on the update, so we will be over writing it with the default for the field (empty string). 

Can we add a check for holder identity after the release, in your test to make sure that is not happening?
